description: Ask Diderot a question and get back a written answer with citations. Diderot does its own research across the corpus and whatever else the deployment gives it (code, the web, live telemetry), so use this for a question that needs several sources weighed together or an investigation, and use `retrieve` and `list` when you want the raw material yourself. Write the question so it stands alone: Diderot sees nothing of your conversation. Say whose work or which system you mean, the period, and the form of answer you need. The call starts an asynchronous task; poll it with tasks/get until it completes, which can take a few minutes. The result carries `session_id`: pass it back as `session_id` to ask a follow-up in the same conversation, where Diderot still has the earlier question, its research and its answer. Images the answer produced are listed under `artifacts` and returned as resource links; fetch one with resources/read on its `uri`.

question.description: The question, written to stand alone: name the people, systems and period you mean, and the form of answer you need.

session_id.description: The 'session_id' of an earlier ask result of yours, to continue that conversation. Omit to start a new one.

name: ask

description: Fetch one attachment that an `expand` result lists under `attachments`, by its `id`. An image comes back as image content together with its caption. A document (PDF, DOCX, XLSX) comes back as its extracted text under `text`; when `next_offset` is present the text continues, so call again with that value as `offset`. When content is missing or incomplete (an image over 4 MB, an image not stored yet, a document not extracted yet or extracted only in part), `note` says why, and the caption, if there is one, is still included.

id.description: The id of an entry in an expand result's attachments.

offset.description: For a document: the next_offset of the previous call, to continue its text.

name: attachment

description: Read the full source behind one result: pass the `event_id` of a `retrieve` or `list` hit. Use it when the answer depends on something the hit does not show: the rest of a thread, the exact text of a command or an error, a decision further down a page. What comes back depends on the source. For slack: the whole thread, or, for a message with no thread, the messages around it in the channel (up to 20 messages and 30 minutes either side), where a message that started a thread is marked with its reply count and an event_id you can expand in turn. For agent_session: the stretch of the session that a chunk hit summarizes, or, for a session-level hit, the whole session when it is short and otherwise an outline of its stretches, each with a summary and the `event_id` to expand to read that stretch. For notion: the whole page. For linear: the whole issue with its comments. For zendesk: the indexed ticket conversation or article, with the attachment content the asker may see. For discord: the whole thread or forum post, or, for a message outside a thread, the messages around it in its channel and the message it replies to. The result carries the same `actor` object as the hit, and `truncated` when the content was cut to fit. Files attached to the returned messages are listed under `attachments` with name, type, size in bytes and, for an image, its caption. Pass an attachment's `id` to `attachment` to get the image or the document's text. An item named exactly in a `retrieve` question has already been read through this same path and comes back under its `references`, marked `truncated` when it was cut to fit, so do not expand to find it. When `supported` is false, `note` says why (the event cannot be read from here, or its source cannot be expanded right now): work from the hit you have, as you should when the call returns an error. Results can run to tens of kilobytes, so expand the hits that matter, not every hit.

event_id.description: The event_id of a retrieve or list result.

name: expand

description:
List every event that matches a set of filters, newest first, with no relevance ranking. Use it when the question is about a set and not a topic: what a person did in a period, every agent session on a day, each thread in a channel last week. To find the best matches for a topic, use `retrieve`.

At least one of `sources`, `actors`, `channels`, `occurred_after` or `occurred_before` is required. Each row is a whole event, not a passage, with its content cut to about 2,000 characters, or about 1,100 when a page holds 50 rows; `truncated` marks a cut row. For slack, discord, notion, linear and zendesk, `expand` returns the whole item. A cut agent-session summary cannot be completed that way (`expand` returns the session itself), so ask for 25 rows or fewer to get more of each summary. When more events match than fit in one response it carries `next_cursor`: pass that back as `cursor`, with the same filters, for the next page. A response that carries `next_cursor` is not the whole set. Narrow the filters before paging far.

To read a Slack or Discord channel, pass `channels` with a time range. Messages come newest first, up to 50 per call; a reply has `is_reply: true` and shares its root's `thread_id`. In a busy channel or over a long range, set `thread_roots_only` to get one row per conversation, then `expand` the threads that matter. This is also the way to find a message someone remembers by who posted it, where and roughly when, which `retrieve` cannot do.

For agent sessions, set `session_level_only` to get one row per session and not one per stretch of each session. `expand` on a session-level row returns the whole session when it is short and otherwise an outline of its stretches, each with an `event_id` to expand.

In each row, `actor` is an object: `display` is the name to use in prose; `canonical` ({namespace,id}) is the person's identity across sources, and when its namespace is `email` its id is the value to pass back in an `actors` filter, copied exactly; `source_identity` ({namespace,id}) is the source's own id for the person; and `role` says what the person is to the item: message_author for slack and discord (the sharer, for a file or an image), session_owner for agent_session, last_editor for notion (who may not be the author), issue_creator for linear, and event_actor for zendesk (the ticket's requester, a comment's author or an article's author). `occurred_at` is when a slack or discord message was posted. A discord actor's canonical identity is the Discord account (namespace `discord_user`), never an email, so it does not match the same person in other sources. For notion and linear it is the last update, which does not date the events the text describes. For agent_session, a chunk result is dated by the last record of its stretch and a session-level result by the session's last activity.

sources.description: Limit the list to these sources. 'slack' = indexed channel messages plus messages sent directly to Diderot; one-to-one and group DMs between other people are never indexed. 'discord' = messages, threads and forum posts from the Discord server channels this deployment indexes. 'agent_session' = canonical summaries of redacted coding-agent session transcripts. Use agent_session for technical, engineering, research, review, and operational work, including reasoning and resolutions that may not appear in slack. 'notion' = internal Notion pages: docs, runbooks, specs, design/product docs, and structured database rows. Use notion for documented decisions, processes, specs, and reference material. 'linear' = engineering issue tracker: tasks, bugs, projects, and their discussion threads. 'zendesk' = indexed customer support tickets, individual replies/internal notes, and Help Center articles with available attachment content. Use zendesk for support reports and guidance, not engineering work items. 'markdown' = Markdown documents from a folder this deployment indexes. 'imap' = Email messages from an owner's IMAP mailboxes. 'caldav' = Calendar events and journal notes from an owner's CalDAV collections.

actors.description: Limit the list to events by these people. Give each as a full email address (the canonical id of one of their results, or, in Ask, asker.email from the context block): an email matches the same person in every source. A display name matches only if it is exactly the name the source stores, so a first name alone usually matches nothing, and a filter that matches no one returns no rows and no error.

channels.description: Limit the list to messages in these Slack or Discord channels. Each entry is a channel name (with or without '#'), a channel ID, or a link to the channel or one of its messages. A Discord channel includes its threads and forum posts. A channel that does not exist, or that the caller cannot read, is an error.

occurred_after.description: RFC 3339 time. Only events at or after it.

occurred_before.description: RFC 3339 time. Only events at or before it.

thread_roots_only.description: For slack and discord: return only top-level messages (thread roots and messages with no thread), one row per conversation, leaving out replies.

session_level_only.description: For agent_session: return one row per session (its whole-session summary), leaving out the rows for each stretch of a session.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of the previous response, passed unchanged with the same filters, to get the next page. Leave it unset for the first page.

name: list

description:
Semantic search over the organization's corpus. Returns the passages that best match `question`, each with its source, actor, time and, when it has one, a url. Use it to find what was said, decided or done about a topic. To enumerate everything that matches a filter, or to read a Slack or Discord channel over a period, use `list`.

The search ranks by meaning, not by matching words, so describe what you are looking for in the words the content would use. Quotation marks, minus signs, boolean operators and filters written into `question` do nothing: restrict a search with `sources`, `actors` and the time parameters. With `sources` unset, or naming several, each source is ranked on its own and the best `top_k` of each come back, so a small source is not crowded out by a large one: begin with that. Name one source to get more from it. The nearest passages are always returned, however weak, so a hit is not proof of relevance: judge it by its text. An empty result means the filters excluded everything, most often an `actors` value that matches no one or a time bound: loosen them. It never shows that the thing does not exist.

Each hit carries:
- `event_id`: pass it to `expand` to read the full source.
- `actor` is an object: `display` is the name to use in prose; `canonical` ({namespace,id}) is the person's identity across sources, and when its namespace is `email` its id is the value to pass back in an `actors` filter, copied exactly; `source_identity` ({namespace,id}) is the source's own id for the person; and `role` says what the person is to the item: message_author for slack and discord (the sharer, for a file or an image), session_owner for agent_session, last_editor for notion (who may not be the author), issue_creator for linear, and event_actor for zendesk (the ticket's requester, a comment's author or an article's author). `occurred_at` is when a slack or discord message was posted. A discord actor's canonical identity is the Discord account (namespace `discord_user`), never an email, so it does not match the same person in other sources. For notion and linear it is the last update, which does not date the events the text describes. For agent_session, a chunk result is dated by the last record of its stretch and a session-level result by the session's last activity.
- `channel` (slack): the channel's name; a discord hit's `title` names its channel and thread. `has_thread` (slack, discord): what `expand` returns, the whole thread when true and the surrounding messages in the channel when false.
- `granularity` (agent_session): `chunk` for a summary of one stretch of a session, `session` for a summary of a whole session. Expanding a chunk returns that stretch of the session itself, which is where exact commands and output are. Expanding a session-level hit returns the whole session when it is short and otherwise an outline of its stretches, each with an `event_id` to expand.
- `content_kind`: present when the text is not the actor's own words. `image_caption` is a model's description of an image they shared. `document_text` is text extracted from a file they attached: `document` names the file, and `document_completeness: partial` means part of it is missing (`document_pages` and `document_pages_extracted` give the coverage). Attribute such text to the image or the file ("contract.pdf, shared by Sam in #legal"), not to the actor.

An exact handle in the question is read directly, as well as searched for: a Slack message link, a Linear issue URL, an
issue key such as ENG-123 for a Linear team the corpus indexes, a session UUID, 'event_id: N', 'chunk_id: N', or a
Zendesk ticket or article URL. Each comes back under 'references', ahead of the hits, with the handle as written, its
kind, event_id, source, url when it has one, content, and truncated when the content was cut to fit. If any handle
cannot be read for this caller, the whole call fails with "I couldn't access the referenced corpus item." and returns no hits; ask
again without that handle to search by topic.

question.description: What to look for, as a descriptive phrase or sentence with the distinctive terms and enough context to tell it apart. A one-word query retrieves poorly.

sources.description: Limit the search to these sources. With none given, every source is searched, each ranked on its own. 'slack' = indexed channel messages plus messages sent directly to Diderot; one-to-one and group DMs between other people are never indexed. 'discord' = messages, threads and forum posts from the Discord server channels this deployment indexes. 'agent_session' = canonical summaries of redacted coding-agent session transcripts. Use agent_session for technical, engineering, research, review, and operational work, including reasoning and resolutions that may not appear in slack. 'notion' = internal Notion pages: docs, runbooks, specs, design/product docs, and structured database rows. Use notion for documented decisions, processes, specs, and reference material. 'linear' = engineering issue tracker: tasks, bugs, projects, and their discussion threads. 'zendesk' = indexed customer support tickets, individual replies/internal notes, and Help Center articles with available attachment content. Use zendesk for support reports and guidance, not engineering work items. 'markdown' = Markdown documents from a folder this deployment indexes. 'imap' = Email messages from an owner's IMAP mailboxes. 'caldav' = Calendar events and journal notes from an owner's CalDAV collections.

actors.description: Limit the search to events by these people. Give each as a full email address (the canonical id of one of their results, or, in Ask, asker.email from the context block): an email matches the same person in every source. The source's own id for a person (source_identity.id of one of their results) also matches, in that source only. A display name does not match here: use list to filter by an exact display name, or take the email from one of the person's results. A filter that matches no one returns no hits and no error.

occurred_after.description: RFC 3339 time. Only events from this time on. Bound a search by time only when the question names a period or needs recent material, because a bound hides older content that may still hold.

occurred_before.description: RFC 3339 time. Only events up to this time.

top_k.description: How many passages to return. With one source named: that many from it, 20 by default. With several or none: that many from each source, 5 by default and 10 at most.

name: retrieve
